av_event.what: Her eyes drop away from the screen towards the window on her left and stay there for a couple of seconds. Her mouth presses into a tight line and her shoulders rise and fall with a slow breath out through her nose before she looks back at the screen.

text:
B: Hello? Yeah, you're on.
A: Hello. I'm Shazia.
B: Tracey. Dagenham, East London.
A: Blackburn.
B: Blackburn. Never been. Is it nice?
A: It's alright. It's home, sort of.
B: Yeah. Same as Dagenham, really. It's changed a lot, mind. Where I grew up, everyone's dad was at Ford's, my dad was, and now half the street I don't know who they are. Not being funny, it's just different. D'you know what I mean.
A: Mm.
B: So, erm, you working?
A: No. Not since the warehouse. My back.
B: Oh, that's rubbish. I clean offices, evenings. My back's not great neither, all them bins.
A: Do you like it?
B: It's alright. Nobody bothers you once they've all gone home. Supervisor's a pain, mind. Always picking on something. Last month he had a go at me about one floor. One floor, out of the whole building, and I'd done all the toilets and the kitchen. I was fuming about it all week.
A: They always find something.
B: They do! That's what I said to Gary.
A: I had one like that. At the agency. Every time I was five minutes late, straight on the phone.
B: Five minutes!
A: Well. Sometimes more.
B: Ha. Yeah, well. It's the buses, ain't it. The 5's never on time.
A: Ours are the same. And the bins. They didn't come again this week, whole street's full.
B: Don't. Council's useless. Our landlord won't sort the damp in the bathroom neither. I've rung him four times.
A: Gas and electric as well. It's too much now.
B: Tell me about it. Weekly shop at Asda, I nearly cried last week. So what d'you do all day, then, if you're not working?
A: Erm, I go to my mum's. I do these surveys, online. For vouchers.
B: Oh, I do them! The survey apps. I've got about four on my phone. Is that how you found this?
A: Yeah. Imran said it was a scam.
B: Gary said the same! He says nobody pays you to sit and chat. Is that your husband, Imran?
A: Yeah. Taxi driver. We've not got kids, so my aunties, every time I see them, it's when, when. Eight years now.
B: Yeah.
A: They don't let it drop.
B: Families, ain't it. I don't speak to my sister no more. Four years. Over my nan's will.
A: Four years?
B: Yeah. Her fault, not mine. Anyway. What else d'you do?
A: I watch dramas. And I doodle. On envelopes, that kind of thing.
B: You're joking. I do that! Faces, mostly. I was good at Art at school. Got a C.
A: I got a C in art as well.
B: Look at us. Is that it, then, are we meant to keep going till it...
